source_vintage_and_cutoff.summary: Information cutoff: 23 Nov 2026 06:20 BRT. NBS industrial production release is dated 17 Nov; China Mining Association customs summary 16 Nov; NBS fixed-asset and economic releases 17/16 Nov; SteelHome inventory survey 19 Nov; Reuters steel-market observation 23 Nov 01:53 GMT; Pilbara Ports 13 Nov; SimFer project update 6 Aug; Guinea government note 19 Nov; Reuters French PMI 23 Nov 05:18 BRT; Reuters Asian oil quote 23 Nov 05:44 BRT. World Steel October production data was not yet available, so the report uses September observations and explicitly labels the 24 Nov release as future.

factual_methodology.summary: NBS confirms Jan-Oct crude steel 795.61 Mt (-2.8%), pig iron 691.52 Mt (-3.1%), rolled steel 1,173.48 Mt (-2.6%) and October crude steel 70.83 Mt (-1.6%). China Mining Association, citing GACC, reports iron-ore imports 1,060.554 Mt (+3.1%). SteelHome survey reports 157.36 Mt at 46 main ports, +1.16 Mt weekly, with ~110 Mt held by traders. Reuters/Mysteel supports around 10% of surveyed mills profitable versus 38% a year earlier, six consecutive weekly hot-metal declines to ~2.3 Mt/day, and the specified intraday DCE/SGX prices. Brazil's official MDIC consolidated October product data confirms US$2.124bn and 36.5 Mt, down 27.6% in value and 8.9% in volume; unit value US$58.1/t and -20.5%. Pilbara Ports confirms Port Hedland 48.0 Mt iron-ore exports (-4% y/y). SimFer reports 2.2 Mt shipped H1, rail commissioned Q1, mine progress 77%, port infrastructure 85% and Q1 2027 commissioning expectation. Guinea's 19 Nov note says sovereign-fund ratification was examined, not completed. Reuters supports France Composite PMI 46.2 and the time-stamped Brent/WTI quote. Evidence is not used to claim a structural ore surplus or an imminent price collapse.

evidence_traceability.summary: Both editions contain the same 23 unique reference URLs. Core physical-flow claims draw on NBS, GACC-derived customs data, SteelHome and Pilbara Ports. Brazil export calculations are supported by official MDIC consolidated commodity data. SimFer project progress and Guinea institutional status rely on project and government sources. Reuters market values and PMI observations are separately time-stamped; future global steel data are not represented as already published.

The European Commission 2026–2028 forecasts and Nvidia's next-quarter guidance are projections, while October Eurostat/ONS figures are observed outcomes.

en.deck: Chinese iron-ore imports rose 3.1% in January–October while crude-steel output fell 2.8%; inventories, margins and new export corridors now determine how the adjustment reaches producers.

signal_rationale.delta: The latest available editions focused on AI productivity/valuation, cross-asset stress and energy security. This issue adds a distinct physical-trade signal: Chinese iron-ore imports are rising while steel and pig-iron output fall, with port inventories and exporter receipts showing where the adjustment is being absorbed.
signal_rationale.evidence: GACC-derived imports +3.1% y/y Jan–Oct; NBS crude steel −2.8%, pig iron −3.1%; SteelHome port inventory +1.16 Mt w/w; Brazil iron-ore export value −27.6% y/y; Port Hedland iron-ore exports −4% y/y; SimFer shipped 2.2 Mt in H1.
signal_rationale.scale_path: China’s procurement and stock management affect seaborne ore prices; Brazil and Australia transmit price changes through export receipts; Guinea’s rail-port corridor adds future supply while its fiscal institutions remain in process.
signal_rationale.transmission: Steel margins and hot-metal output → procurement and inventories → benchmark ore prices and unit values → exporter cash flow, tax receipts and marginal infrastructure finance; energy and freight costs affect delivered costs in parallel.
signal_rationale.falsifier: A sustained decline in port and mill inventories together with rising hot-metal output and improving steel margins would weaken the inventory-led adjustment thesis.

key_constraints: Global October steel production was not yet released at the 06:20 BRT cut-off; September is the latest complete global comparison.
The port-stock figure is a SteelHome industry survey, not a complete official inventory census.
Ore imports and steel output are not directly comparable because of grades, domestic ore, stock changes and shipment timing.
Brazil product-level export values are calculated from MDIC Comex Stat NCM 2601 data.
The latest comparable global credit-spread observation was not available at the cut-off; ECB risk statements are qualitative.
Guinea’s sovereign-fund law was still in a ratification process; no capitalization or operational status was established.
